# D5 Gap-Closing Round 3

Issue #602. Four deficits from the honest accounting, attacked root-cause-first.
Protocol: same splits, fixed seeds, mboostrs vs CatBoost/LightGBM/XGBoost.
Every number below is from an executed cell.

import time
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
from sklearn.datasets import load_breast_cancer, load_diabetes
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.metrics import log_loss, mean_squared_error
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression, Ridge
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
import mboostrs as mb
import catboost, lightgbm, xgboost
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

SEED = 602
print("mboostrs:", mb.__file__)

## Deficit 3: Cancer panel

Wisconsin breast cancer (n=569, p=30), binary classification, log-loss.
Prior: +108.7% excess. #509 diagnosed mstop overshoot (overfitting).

X, y = load_breast_cancer(return_X_y=True)

def run_cancer(seed):
    Xtr, Xte, ytr, yte = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=seed)
    df_tr = pl.DataFrame({f"x{i}": Xtr[:, i] for i in range(30)}).with_columns(pl.Series("y", ytr))
    df_te = pl.DataFrame({f"x{i}": Xte[:, i] for i in range(30)}).with_columns(pl.Series("y", yte))
    formula = "y ~ " + " + ".join(f"bbs(x{i})" for i in range(30))
    out = {}
    for name, ms in [("mb_200", 200), ("mb_500", 500)]:
        m = mb.gamboost(formula, data=df_tr, family=mb.Binomial(),
                        control=mb.boost_control(mstop=ms))
        p = np.clip(m.predict(df_te), 1e-6, 1-1e-6)
        out[name] = log_loss(yte, p)
    cb = catboost.CatBoostClassifier(iterations=200, depth=4, learning_rate=0.05,
                                     random_seed=seed, verbose=False).fit(Xtr, ytr)
    out["catboost"] = log_loss(yte, np.clip(cb.predict_proba(Xte)[:, 1], 1e-6, 1-1e-6))
    lgb = lightgbm.LGBMClassifier(n_estimators=200, max_depth=4, learning_rate=0.05,
                                  random_state=seed, verbose=-1).fit(Xtr, ytr)
    out["lightgbm"] = log_loss(yte, np.clip(lgb.predict_proba(Xte)[:, 1], 1e-6, 1-1e-6))
    lr = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000).fit(Xtr, ytr)
    out["logreg"] = log_loss(yte, lr.predict_proba(Xte)[:, 1])
    return out

for seed in [0, 1, 2]:
    r = run_cancer(seed)
    best = min(r["catboost"], r["lightgbm"])
    excess = (r["mb_200"] - best) / best * 100
    print(f"seed {seed}: mb={r['mb_200']:.4f} cb={r['catboost']:.4f} lgb={r['lightgbm']:.4f} "
          f"logreg={r['logreg']:.4f} excess={excess:.0f}%")

### Root cause: Binomial coefficients don't match the MLE

mboostrs's Binomial boosting finds coefficients with only r=0.23 correlation
to sklearn's logistic regression. Gaussian boosting is fine (competitive with
Ridge on diabetes). The problem is Binomial-specific — the boosting update
for the logit link is not converging to the right solution.

# Coefficient comparison
Xtr, Xte, ytr, yte = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=0)
df_tr = pl.DataFrame({f"x{i}": Xtr[:, i] for i in range(30)}).with_columns(pl.Series("y", ytr))
m = mb.gamboost("y ~ " + " + ".join(f"bols(x{i})" for i in range(30)),
                data=df_tr, family=mb.Binomial(),
                control=mb.boost_control(mstop=500))
c = m.coef()
def get_slope(v):
    return float(v[1]) if isinstance(v, (list, np.ndarray)) and len(v) > 1 else 0.0
mb_beta = np.array([get_slope(c[f"x{i}"]) for i in range(30)])
lr = LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000, C=1e6).fit(Xtr, ytr)
print(f"mboostrs beta norm: {np.linalg.norm(mb_beta):.1f}")
print(f"sklearn beta norm: {np.linalg.norm(lr.coef_[0]):.1f}")
print(f"correlation: {np.corrcoef(mb_beta, lr.coef_[0])[0, 1]:.2f}")

# Gaussian sanity check
Xd, yd = load_diabetes(return_X_y=True)
Xtr, Xte, ytr, yte = train_test_split(Xd, yd, test_size=0.3, random_state=0)
df_tr = pl.DataFrame({f"x{i}": Xtr[:, i] for i in range(10)}).with_columns(pl.Series("y", ytr))
df_te = pl.DataFrame({f"x{i}": Xte[:, i] for i in range(10)}).with_columns(pl.Series("y", yte))
m = mb.gamboost("y ~ " + " + ".join(f"bols(x{i})" for i in range(10)),
                data=df_tr, family=mb.Gaussian(),
                control=mb.boost_control(mstop=500))
ridge = Ridge().fit(Xtr, ytr)
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error
print(f"\nmboostrs Gaussian MSE: {mean_squared_error(yte, m.predict(df_te)):.0f}")
print(f"Ridge MSE: {mean_squared_error(yte, ridge.predict(Xte)):.0f}")

**Verdict: FILED AS STRUCTURAL.** The Binomial boosting update needs
investigation (gradient/link handling). Filed as a separate issue; not a
tuning or model-form problem.
